name: Adult Familial Nephronophthisis-Spastic Quadriparesia Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Adult Familial Nephronophthisis-Spastic Quadriparesia Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of corticomedullary cystic kidney disease consistent with nephronophthisis
Clinical evidence of spastic quadriparesis with upper motor neuron signs
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with nephronophthisis and spasticity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of corticomedullary cystic kidney disease and clinical spastic quadriparesis, with or without genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can aid diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and imaging criteria are met.

searchTerms: kidney cysts near cortex and medulla
stiffness and weakness in all limbs
difficulty moving arms and legs due to stiffness

pathognomonic.symptomName: Polyuria and polydipsia due to impaired renal concentrating ability

common.symptomName: Progressive chronic kidney disease leading to renal failure
Muscle stiffness and spasticity predominantly affecting limbs
searchTerms: muscle tightness in arms and legs
inability to hold urine at night
involuntary muscle contractions after tendon tap

occasional.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: low red blood cells from kidney disease

occasional.symptomName: Bladder dysfunction with urgency and incontinence

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and urea indicating renal impairment
Urinalysis showing isosthenuria and mild proteinuria
imaging: Ultrasound showing corticomedullary cysts and small echogenic kidneys
MRI brain may show mild cerebral atrophy
Spinal MRI may reveal corticospinal tract involvement
genetic: Pathogenic variants in NPHP genes (e.g., NPHP1, NPHP4)
Mutations associated with hereditary spastic paraplegia genes in some cases
other: Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Neurological examination revealing spasticity and hyperreflexia

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly lower limb spasticity without renal involvement
Absence of corticomedullary cystic kidney disease
Earlier onset in childhood or adolescence
More rapid progression to end-stage renal disease

redFlags: Rapidly progressive renal failure in young adult
Onset of spastic quadriparesis with upper motor neuron signs
Family history of renal cystic disease and neurological impairment
references: Orphanet: Adult Familial Nephronophthisis-Spastic Quadriparesia Syndrome, ORPHA:2666
Hildebrandt F, et al. Nephronophthisis: disease mechanisms of a ciliopathy. J Am Soc Nephrol. 2009
Parisi MA. Clinical and molecular features of nephronophthisis and related ciliopathies. Pediatr Nephrol. 2009
